2. //
3. // Demonstrates WHY the original single-expression idiom
4. //     inner.bitmap.number_of_bits() - inner.bitmap.usage()
5. // must be split into named `let nbits` / `let used` bindings.
6. //
7. // The key to faithfulness is the MODULE BOUNDARY: the real `::bitmap::Bitmap`
8. // has a `closed spec fn view` defined in a *different crate*, so
9. // `inner.bitmap@.num_bits` is OPAQUE in `frame.rs` — its `>= 0` lower bound is
10. // not visible. Here `Bitmap` lives in an inner `mod bm` and is called from
11. // outside, so its closed view is likewise hidden (closed-spec bodies are visible
12. // only within their defining module). A same-module model would leak
13. // `num_bits == self.n as int >= 0` and FAIL to reproduce the failure.
14. //
15. //   * `number_of_bits()` postcondition `result as int == num_bits` is the ONLY
16. //     place the caller learns `num_bits == nbits (a usize) >= 0`.
17. //   * `lemma_free_count` REQUIRES `b@.num_bits >= 0` (== frame.proof.rs:95).
18. //
19. // PASS form (`free_count_split`): `let nbits = number_of_bits()` materializes the
20. //   `usize`/`u32` value, so `nbits as int == num_bits` and `nbits >= 0` discharge
21. //   the lemma precondition. Verifies.
22. // FAIL form (`free_count_inline`, shipped COMMENTED OUT): the lemma runs before
23. //   any binding materializes the usize fact, so `num_bits >= 0` is unknown.

48. // `Bitmap` lives behind a module boundary so its closed view is hidden from the
49. // caller — mirroring the real cross-crate `::bitmap` boundary.
50. mod bm {
51.     use vstd::prelude::*;
52. 
53.     pub struct BitmapView {
54.         pub num_bits: int,
55.         pub usage: int,
56.     }
57. 
58.     pub struct Bitmap {
59.         n: u32,
60.         u: u32,
61.     }
62. 
63.     impl View for Bitmap {
64.         type V = BitmapView;
65.         closed spec fn view(&self) -> BitmapView {
66.             BitmapView { num_bits: self.n as int, usage: self.u as int }
67.         }
68.     }
69. 
70.     impl Bitmap {
71.         pub closed spec fn inv(&self) -> bool {
72.             self.u <= self.n
73.         }
74. 
75.         // == ::bitmap number_of_bits(): the `usize`/`u32` result postcondition is
76.         // the ONLY materialization point of `num_bits >= 0` for a caller.
77.         pub fn number_of_bits(&self) -> (result: u32)
78.             requires self.inv(),
79.             ensures result as int == self@.num_bits,
80.         {
81.             self.n
82.         }
83. 
84.         pub fn usage(&self) -> (result: u32)
85.             requires self.inv(),
86.             ensures result as int == self@.usage,
87.         {
88.             self.u
89.         }
90.     }
91. }
92.

94. 
95. // == frame.proof.rs lemma_free_count: REQUIRES the opaque `num_bits >= 0`.
96. pub proof fn lemma_free_count(b: &Bitmap)
97.     requires
98.         b.inv(),
99.         b@.num_bits >= 0,
100. {
101. }
102. 
103. // ---- PASS form: split bindings materialize `num_bits >= 0` ----
104. pub fn free_count_split(b: &Bitmap) -> (result: u32)
105.     requires
106.         b.inv(),
107.         b@.usage <= b@.num_bits,
108. {
109.     let nbits: u32 = b.number_of_bits();
110.     let used: u32 = b.usage();
111.     proof! { lemma_free_count(b); }
112.     nbits - used
113. }
114. 
115. // ---- FAIL form (uncomment to reproduce): inlined expression ----
116. // The lemma runs before any binding surfaces the usize fact, so `num_bits >= 0`
